issues.legal_issue: A post-execution alteration that adds marginal witnesses to an agreement does not invalidate it when the alteration does not change its legal effect or prejudice a party bound by it.
material_facts: The agreement for sale was not invalid in its original form and did not require marginal witnesses to be legally valid.
The alteration at issue was the addition of two names as marginal witnesses; the lower courts had not treated the addition as undermining the claim based on the agreement.
The Supreme Court considered the effect of the alteration even assuming it had been made after execution.
issues.conclusion: The addition of the marginal witnesses was not a material alteration and did not affect the validity or enforceability of the agreement for sale.
issues.legal_principle: Under the principle stated in Halsbury’s Laws of England and reflected in M.S. Anirudhan v. Thomco’s Bank Ltd. and Kaliana Gounder v. Palani Gounder, an alteration is material if it varies the parties’ rights or legal position, changes the instrument’s legal effect, or otherwise prejudices the party bound by it. An alteration that does none of these things does not invalidate the instrument. The agreement did not require marginal witnesses for validity. The decree for specific performance was made in the context of the courts’ discretionary jurisdiction under Section 20 of the Specific Relief Act.

rule.if: specific_performance_dispute and agreement_valid_without_attestation and alteration_added_witness_names and alteration_did_not_change_legal_effect and alteration_did_not_prejudice_bound_party

predicates.specific_performance_dispute: The proceeding concerns a claim to enforce an agreement for sale.
predicates.agreement_valid_without_attestation: The agreement was legally valid without the marginal witnesses whose names were later added.
predicates.alteration_added_witness_names: Names of marginal witnesses were added to the agreement after its execution.
predicates.alteration_did_not_change_legal_effect: The addition did not vary the parties’ rights or change the legal effect of the agreement.
predicates.alteration_did_not_prejudice_bound_party: The addition did not otherwise prejudice a party bound by the agreement.

issues.definition: When a specific-performance dispute involves an agreement that was valid without attesting witnesses, adding witness names does not prevent enforcement if the addition changes neither the agreement’s legal effect nor the position of a party bound by it.

issues.legal_issue: A High Court exercising second-appellate jurisdiction cannot set aside concurrent findings of fact on an issue not raised in the appeal or shown to disclose an error of law.
material_facts: The trial court and first appellate court concurrently accepted the claim based on the agreement for sale and rejected the competing claim.
The lower courts had considered the alleged addition of marginal witnesses but did not treat it as a substantial ground against the agreement.
The High Court’s second appeals had been admitted on a question concerning statutory protections for transferees, but that question was not pressed.

The High Court nevertheless reversed the concurrent decisions on the basis of its own finding about the alleged alteration, an issue not raised in the memorandum of appeal or presented in that form to the lower courts.
The High Court did not identify a legal error by the lower courts supporting its interference.
issues.conclusion: The High Court’s interference was contrary to Section 100 of the Code of Civil Procedure and unsustainable; its judgment was set aside and the concurrent decisions of the lower courts were restored.
issues.legal_principle: Section 100 of the Code of Civil Procedure confines second appeals to substantial questions of law. A second appellate court cannot upset concurrent findings by deciding an issue not raised in the appeal or in that form before the lower courts, without identifying a legal error warranting interference. A finding based on surmise does not justify disturbing those decisions.

rule.if: second_appeal and concurrent_lower_court_findings and reversal_based_on_unraised_issue and no_legal_error_in_lower_decisions_shown

predicates.second_appeal: The proceeding is a second appeal from a decision of a lower appellate court.
predicates.concurrent_lower_court_findings: The trial court and first appellate court reached the same material findings.
predicates.reversal_based_on_unraised_issue: The second appellate court reversed on an issue not raised in the appeal or presented in that form before the lower courts.
predicates.no_legal_error_in_lower_decisions_shown: No legal error in the lower courts’ decisions was identified as a basis for reversal.

issues.definition: In a second appeal, concurrent findings cannot be set aside on an unraised issue when no legal error in the lower courts’ decisions is shown.
